title: Reactivate response reports a reactivation even for no-op calls
reasoning: The handler mutates state by recording a heartbeat, then chooses the response message from the final active/disabled state. Because the message only checks `not settings.schedules_auto_disabled` after the mutation, a request made while schedules were already active still returns `"Schedules reactivated"`, so clients cannot distinguish an actual reactivation from an idempotent no-op.
reproduction: Call `POST /reactivate` when `schedules_auto_disabled` is already false; the response still includes `message: "Schedules reactivated"`.
recommendation: Capture whether schedules were auto-disabled before calling the state-changing operation, or have the service return an explicit `reactivated` flag, and only emit the reactivation message when a transition occurred.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and no route test was found that asserts the no-op `/reactivate` response.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test for `POST /reactivate` when schedules are already active and assert the response does not claim a reactivation occurred.
minimumFixScope: Update `reactivate_schedules` and, if needed, the activity tracker return contract to expose whether the call actually re-enabled schedules.
